ios.desc:
You opened Instagram to reply to a message, opened X to check one notification, opened Reddit to look up one thing.

Then, somehow, thirty minutes disappeared.

Most screen time apps try to solve this with blockers, timers, or daily limits. They assume the problem is that these apps are too accessible.

But that’s rarely what happens.

You didn’t intend to spend half an hour scrolling. Somewhere along the way, your intention changed.

Haserupt helps you hold on to that intention.

Before opening a distracting app, Hase asks what you’re there to do. Whether you’re replying to messages, checking updates, or posting something, Hase gives you just enough time to finish your task. Afterwards, he helps you resist the urge to jump right back in, making it easier to avoid another endless scrolling session.

It doesn’t stop you from using your favourite apps.

It helps you stop using them without meaning to.

Over time, Hase gets to know your habits, celebrates your progress, and gently nudges you back on track whenever your attention starts to drift. Instead of feeling like another app that’s trying to control you, Hase feels like a companion who’s quietly cheering you on.

With Haserupt, you can:

• Leave social media when you planned to.
• Spend less time falling into endless feeds.
• Stay connected without relying on strict blockers or daily limits.
• Build healthier screen habits that actually last.
• See your relationship with your phone improve over time.

Because the problem was never opening the app.

It was forgetting why you opened it in the first place.

quotes.text:
Instead of daily limits or scheduled focus sessions, Haserupt asks what you’re opening an app for before you open it. It then gives you just enough time to complete that task. Once the timer expires, the app stays unavailable for a short cool-off period. If you genuinely need more time right away, you can explain why and request an extension.
For instance, when you open Instagram, you can choose one amongst "Check DMs (1 min)", "Watch reels (5 mins)", "Long convo (15 min)" and use the app for that much time. After that, Instagram will be locked behind a cooloff. After the cooloff ends, you repeat the process. If you want to reopen during the cooloff, convince the AI companion to let you.

Check it out on the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6763058568

Currently, it's iOS only.
